outcome: The general standard conjectures (Grothendieck's conjectures B, D, and the Hodge standard conjecture) remain open, but Thomas Agugliaro proved the standard conjecture of Hodge type unconditionally for new classes of abelian varieties (powers of abelian threefolds, powers of simple abelian varieties of prime dimension over finite fields, and other Frobenius-rank cases) in a preprint posted 24 October 2025 (arXiv:2510.21562), extending his own 2024 paper (arXiv:2401.17445, to appear in Documenta Mathematica) which constructed infinitely many abelian varieties of dimension g≥5 satisfying the same conjecture.
summary: The triage correctly flagged two 2025 preprints and correctly hedged on whether they count. Having read both in full: arXiv:2508.13882 (Truong, 'Standard conjecture D and some conjectures around Weil's Riemann hypothesis') is explicitly conditional — its main result is 'If Standard conjecture D holds ... then all polarised endomorphisms on X are semisimple,' i.e. it assumes the conjecture and derives consequences, and settles no case of it. This is not a change to the stated problem and is excluded under §3.1. arXiv:2510.21562 (Agugliaro, 'Standard conjecture of Hodge type for powers of abelian varieties'), by contrast, is an unconditional proof of the Hodge standard conjecture (one of the several conjectures collectively called the standard conjectures) for concrete new classes: powers of abelian threefolds, powers of simple abelian varieties of prime dimension over finite fields, and cases characterised by Frobenius rank. This is a genuine restriction of the stated problem (a specific class of varieties) proved true, so it is a case of the problem under §3.1, not a variant — it counts as `partial`, direction `confirmed`. It builds on the same author's 2024 preprint (arXiv:2401.17445, forthcoming in Documenta Mathematica), which had already produced infinitely many g≥5 abelian varieties over finite fields satisfying the conjecture, using a theorem of Ancona on rank-2 motives; that 2024 work is itself in the window (submitted 2024-01-30, after the 26 Jan 2024 freeze — checked and it is one day after, not stale) but the October 2025 paper is the more recent and more general event, so it is the one dated. Neither paper has yet been digested by an expert community (no citations found, no published version, no blog commentary), so under §6.1 this stays short of `resolved`; but it is also not a bare unrefereed claim of a headline result — it is routine, incremental special-case literature of the kind the field regularly produces, and I classify it as `partial` (a case settled) rather than `claimed`, since `claimed` is meant for claims of resolving the (sub)problem that await verification, and here the case genuinely is proved by ordinary rigorous means with no room for a 'the argument might be wrong' concern of the kind `claimed` exists to flag. I also checked adjacent literature that could be mistaken for progress on this problem: Floccari–Varesco (arXiv:2308.04865, v2 Nov 2024, published in Mathematische Annalen 2024) proves the Hodge and Tate CONJECTURES (not the standard conjectures) for 4-dimensional generalized Kummer varieties — a different, related problem, correctly out of scope. Foster (arXiv:2512.04114, Dec 2025) proves the Lefschetz standard conjectures for 4-dimensional Kummer-type varieties, but conditionally on an unproven Buchweitz–Flenner conjecture, so like Truong's paper it does not settle an unconditional case and is excluded. Ito–Ito–Koshikawa's Hodge standard conjecture for self-products of K3 surfaces (arXiv:2206.10086) was posted in June 2022 and has only one arXiv version; its 2025 appearance is solely a journal publication (Journal of Algebraic Geometry) lagging the preprint by three years, which §6.3 explicitly says must not be used as the event date — this result is `open_stale` in isolation, predating the window entirely, and is not the basis for this record's status. No AI system was found anywhere in this literature: none of the four preprints checked (2510.21562, 2508.13882, 2401.17445, 2512.04114) or the two journal papers (2308.04865, 2206.10086) mention any AI system, language model, or automated theorem prover in their abstracts, methodology sections, or (where visible) acknowledgements. Targeted searches for AI/LLM/theorem-prover involvement specific to this problem returned nothing. ai_role is therefore 'none' with an empty basis_quote, as required when no authorial statement exists.
competing_reading: One could argue Agugliaro's result is close enough to routine incremental special-case literature (as the triage worried) that it should not move the status away from 'open' at all, on the theory that the standard conjectures article is really asking about the conjectures in general and cataloguing every proved special case would never let this record read 'open' even though the headline conjecture never moves. I judge against this reading because §3.1 explicitly instructs that 'a single case settled' counts, normally as partial, and does not carve out an exception for fields (like this one) where special cases are proved frequently; the volume of special-case literature is a fact about the field's ordinary variety, not a reason to disregard the instruction.
what_would_settle_it: A citation, referee report, or acceptance of arXiv:2510.21562 by a journal would move it toward being folded into 'resolved for that case' with more confidence, though the status code would still be `partial` since it is not the general conjecture. A subsequent survey or Wikipedia edit explicitly listing this case would also help confirm the classification.
